data.title: Autocomplete
data.tagline: Show matching suggestions while the user types
data.description: Autocomplete works for addresses, contacts, and tags that have common answers but may still allow free text. The user can choose a suggestion or keep typing. If only listed values are valid, use a searchable Select instead.

distinctions.label: Select
distinctions.explanation: Autocomplete offers matches based on what someone types. Select needs no typing and chooses only from a fixed list.

distinctions.label: Combobox
distinctions.explanation: A combobox is the complete control of an input plus a popup option list. Autocomplete emphasizes the behavior of showing matches as someone types; component libraries often use the terms differently.

avoid: Force a suggestion when free text should remain valid
Show unrelated results before enough text is entered
Change the typed value without clear confirmation
Use it for a tiny fixed list

lessonPractice.title: To invite Wang Xiaoming among thousands of employees, which interaction fits?

options.label: Offer matching suggestions after typing, then select an existing employee
options.feedback: Correct. With a large, standardized candidate set, autocomplete supports search and avoids misspelling.

options.label: Put every employee in one long Select
options.feedback: Large option sets are hard to browse and not fast to narrow by name.

options.label: Accept arbitrary text and create a new employee with that name
options.feedback: The invitee must match an existing account; arbitrary creation makes duplicates or wrong targets.

data.agentPrompt: For member invite, query matching employees after at least two characters and send the invite only after a suggestion is selected. Test no result, same-name candidates, and keyboard selection: explain no result, distinguish duplicate names, and submit an employee id after selection.
